name: Joe Biden
role: 46th U.S. president (2021-2025); vice president (2009-2017); U.S. senator from Delaware (1973-2009)
summary: Biden is a Democratic centre-left liberal whose record favours unions, a higher minimum wage, higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations, expanded health coverage, climate investment and civil and LGBTQ+ rights, within a capitalist, bipartisan-minded framework. He supports abortion rights, gun limits short of a ban on guns, NATO and allied military strength, Israel with a two-state goal, and a tougher but legal-pathway immigration policy. He frames politics as defending democracy and institutions, and warned in 2025 of oligarchy and a 'tech-industrial complex'.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed restoring the 39.6 percent top rate, taxing capital gains over $1 million as income, a 25 percent billionaire minimum tax and a higher corporate rate; signed a 15 percent corporate minimum tax in the IRA.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Condemned Russia's invasion as aggression that threatens the free world and led sanctions to make Putin pay.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: In July 2007 he introduced a rendition bill that 'prohibits rendering individuals to countries that will torture or mistreat them or to secret, extraterritorial prisons', saying commitment to the rule of law is among the most formidable counterterrorism weapons.

notes: Answers rest on his own speeches, orders and signed laws from 2021 to January 2025, plus two Wikipedia articles for record items. His 50-year record changed on several issues (crime and the 1994 bill, the Defense of Marriage Act, the Hyde Amendment, same-sex marriage, the death penalty); the recent clear position is recorded, so same-sex marriage reads +2 on his 2012 and 2022 acts. Statements with no recorded position of his own are null; nothing was filled from party or label. A prior pilot audit was discarded and none of its answers were carried over. Judgment calls: the death penalty (-1: he commuted 37 of 40 federal death sentences but left terrorism and hate-crime cases), expand-fossil-fuels (0, low: both directions), legalize-drugs (-1: pardons and decriminalization talk, not endorsement of legal recreational drugs). He did not commit publicly to nuclear power, tax on inheritances or the Supreme Court beyond term limits in the sources opened, so those are null. Cited sources were opened in this session as full texts (American Presidency Project) or Wikipedia. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind (executive orders, proclamations and administration policy statements are actions); sixteen answers that cited both an action and words were reduced to the action sources with history, per record over words; death-penalty and keep-nuclear-weapons, which rested only on Wikipedia, now cite his 23 December 2024 commutation statement and the State Department's New START extension statement. New from his 36 Senate years (Voteview, ICPSR 14101, and Stanford Congressional Record speeches): tax-inheritance (action), surveillance-ok, torture-always-illegal (words); also shut-down-tax-havens, human-caused-global-warming and prohibit-child-medical-transition from existing presidential sources. His Senate votes on the 1996 Defense of Marriage Act (Yea), the 1994 crime bill and Iraq are recorded in Voteview but the same-sex-marriage and crime answers stay with his later acts. The Miller Center copies of his speeches are declined (duplicates of cited American Presidency Project texts or searched without usable hits). Voteview and the Congressional Record hold far more of his Senate record than is mapped here; positions not settled by those votes and speeches stay null.

booksNotUsed.reason: Miller Center copies of presidential speeches; the major ones (inaugural, joint-session address, State of the Union addresses, farewell, Afghanistan, Ukraine, Hamas) are already cited from the American Presidency Project copies, and the rest were searched by keyword (torture, hate, church and state, nuclear power, transgender, voter ID, conscription, work requirements, tax havens, International Criminal Court, climate, nuclear) with usable hits only on the passages cited.
